_about: fak position rows for the 'decoding' group. dim_id links each to a _taxonomy.json dimension.

rows.axis: Speculative decoding throughput effect across batch sizes (does it survive at high concurrency?)
rows.competitor: EAGLE-3; EAGLE-2 (regresses at batch); vLLM / SGLang / TensorRT-LLM speculative backends
rows.fak_doc: docs/benchmarks/published/HEADLINES.json (67bb976926a C=1 DSpark 171.54/180.92 tok/s); no C=16..64 spec-decode sweep
rows.comparison_note: SINGLE-STREAM SHIPPED, HIGH-CONCURRENCY UNMEASURED: fak now ships opt-in CUDA DSpark speculative decoding on Inkling-2-Mini (1.43x d2 / 1.51x d4 at C=1, 67bb976926a) alongside NativeScheduler batching, but has NOT measured whether speculative speedup survives at high serving batch concurrency (e.g. batch 16-64 vs EAGLE-3). Honest no-claim.

rows.competitor: EAGLE-3; Medusa-2; TensorRT-LLM / vLLM speculative decoding
rows.comparison_note: C1 RATE MEASURED ON RTX 5080 (see spec-decode-speedup 1.51x and acceptance-length-rate 0.70), P50/P99 HTTP ITL DISTRIBUTION UNMEASURED: fak measures C=1 in-process DSpark decode speedups (171.54 tok/s d2 / 180.92 tok/s d4 vs 119.72 plain) plus spec oracle depth 4-8 (294-326 tok/s on f32 KV in rtx5080-inkling2-v060), but has no per-token P50/P99 HTTP ITL comparison vs EAGLE-3.

HW-WITNESSED on RTX 5080 (Inkling-2-Mini-UD-Q3_K_XL, opt-in FAK_INKLING2_SPEC): DSpark depth 4 reaches 180.92 tok/s (1.51x vs plain 119.715 tok/s, capitals prompt; depth 2 reaches 171.535 tok/s = 1.43x, superseding prior 151.65 tok/s). Opt-in and not bit-exact on every prompt; trails EAGLE-3's up-to-4.79x on LLaMA-3.3-70B.

rows.axis: Draft acceptance length / acceptance rate (mean accepted tokens per verify step)
rows.competitor_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.01840 (EAGLE-3 0.80-0.88 acceptance rate, ~4.5-5.0 tok/verify); https://arxiv.org/pdf/2412.19437 (DeepSeek-V3 MTP 0.85)
rows.fak_doc: docs/benchmarks/published/HEADLINES.json (67bb976926a: spec.d2=171.535, spec.d4=180.92 tok/s superseding 5915ef42be); docs/benchmarks/published/aegis-inkling2-spec-decode/RESULTS.md (74/106 drafts = 0.70, 2.40 tok/verify at depth 2)
rows.comparison_note: HW-WITNESSED on RTX 5080 (Inkling-2-Mini DSpark depth 2): 74/106 drafts accepted (0.70 acceptance rate, 2.40 tokens/verify in aegis-inkling2-spec-decode prior to the 67bb976926a verify-kernel climb reaching 171.54 tok/s at d2 and 180.92 tok/s at d4). Trails EAGLE-3 (0.80-0.88 rate, ~4.5-5.0 tokens/verify) and DeepSeek-V3 MTP (0.85-0.90 2nd-token rate).

rows.axis: Breadth of speculative methods supported (draft-model, EAGLE/-2/-3, Medusa, MTP, lookahead, n-gram/prompt-lookup)
rows.fak_doc: docs/benchmarks/published/HEADLINES.json (67bb976926a CUDA DSpark MTP); commits 28b7299a29 & 020586f72c (toolgrammar.ForcedDraft jump-forward); internal/polymodel & internal/spec (CPU tree verify)
rows.comparison_note: PARTIAL COVERAGE SHIPPED, STILL TRAILS SOTA MENU: fak now ships CUDA DSpark drafting (opt-in on Inkling-2-Mini) and deterministic toolgrammar.ForcedDraft jump-forward decoding (020586f72c) plus CPU tree-verify primitives, yet lacks general external draft-target, EAGLE-3, Medusa, and SuffixDecoding/n-gram lookup across models on fak serve.

rows.axis: Retrieval / prompt-lookup (n-gram) drafting for input-grounded tasks
rows.fak_doc: No fak evidence: CLAIMS.md / BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md contain no n-gram, prompt-lookup, or retrieval-drafting claim. fak's PickDrafter selects among drafters but no n-gram/prompt-lookup drafter exists.
rows.comparison_note: REAL GAP fak should measure (it is adjacent to fak's thesis). Prompt-lookup is input-grounded reuse — the SAME family as fak's cross-agent prefix reuse — and needs no draft model, so it is a natural fit for a reuse kernel and worth a measured row. fak has zero evidence today. Competitor value is the up-to-2.8x summarization figure.

rows.axis: Output-distribution losslessness of speculation (greedy and stochastic)
rows.fak_doc: internal/spec SpeculativeGreedy/VerifyTree (greedy CPU bit-exact rollback witness); docs/benchmarks/published/aegis-inkling2-spec-decode/RESULTS.md & HEADLINES.json (RTX 5080 DSpark bit_exact=false)
rows.comparison_note: Parity on the greedy CPU oracle half, WITH HONEST FENCES: (1) internal/spec proves token-identity vs plain greedy decode on the CPU PreNorm path (via KVCache.Evict rollback); (2) on CUDA RTX 5080 Inkling-2-Mini, opt-in DSpark batched verify is NOT bit-exact to single-step decode on all prompts due to GEMM reduction order (diverges at token 65 on capitals; bit_exact=false in HEADLINES.json); (3) distribution-preserving stochastic (temperature>0) rejection sampling parity is unbuilt.

rows.axis: Speculative-decoding behavior under high concurrency / large batch (break-even)
rows.fak_doc: internal/modelengine/nativesched.go & HEADLINES.json; no high-batch speculative scaling sweep yet
rows.comparison_note: GAP: NativeScheduler continuous batching and CUDA cohorts are shipped, and C=1 DSpark spec decode is measured (180.92 tok/s d4), but high-concurrency break-even batch sizing for speculative decoding (e.g. batch 16-64 vs MagicDec / EAGLE-3) is unmeasured.

rows.axis: Constrained/guided decoding per-token overhead (JSON-schema, regex, grammar/CFG)
rows.fak_doc: internal/grammar/batch_bitmask_fsm.go (361b316673) + b2a53f9305 (sorted-vocab trie); internal/agent/inkernel_structured.go; internal/toolgrammar ForcedDraft (28b7299a29, 020586f72c); no XGrammar-2 us/token parity benchmark
rows.comparison_note: MECHANISM SHIPPED, OVERHEAD BENCH UNMEASURED: fak now ships native decode-time logit bitmask FSMs (BatchBitmaskFSM with prefix-skip vocab trie and speculative rollback, 361b316673/b2a53f9305), structured carriers in internal/agent/inkernel_structured.go, and toolgrammar.ForcedDraft jump-forward decoding (020586f72c). However, no per-token microsecond latency benchmark against XGrammar-2 (<40 us/tok) is committed, so verdict stays no-claim.

rows.axis: Grammar/schema compilation latency and cache (cold-start for dynamic agentic schemas)
rows.fak_doc: internal/grammar/batch_bitmask_fsm.go SchemaCompileCache (FIFO schema/vocab compile cache, 361b316673) + internal/grammar/json_schema_mask.go; no cold compile-ms benchmark vs XGrammar-2
rows.comparison_note: CACHE SHIPPED, COMPILE LATENCY UNMEASURED: fak now ships SchemaCompileCache caching compiled *JSONSchemaMask and sorted-vocab tries across decode requests (361b316673, b2a53f9305), alongside content-addressed tool-arg grammar dedup, but has committed no cold compile-time (ms) comparison against XGrammar-2 (~10 ms). Honest no-claim.

rows.axis: Structured-output validity vs reasoning-quality tax (constraint-induced degradation)
rows.fak_doc: internal/grammar + internal/agent/inkernel_structured.go (TestNativeGuidedJSONConstrainsCompletion, TestNativeGuidedRegexConstrainsCompletion, TestNativeStructuredCompleteAndStream); no JSONSchemaBench run
rows.comparison_note: NATIVE STRUCTURED CONSTRAINTS SHIPPED, REASONING-TAX BENCH UNMEASURED: fak now enforces bounded JSON-schema, regex, GBNF, and guided_choice bitmasks during native decode (witnessed by go test ./internal/agent and ./internal/grammar), but has NOT run JSONSchemaBench or ExtractBench to quantify validity-vs-reasoning accuracy loss. Honest no-claim.

rows.axis: Tool/function-call parsing coverage and robustness (per-model formats)
rows.competitor: vLLM tool-call parsers; SGLang; XGrammar-2 (grammar-backed tool calling)
rows.fak_doc: internal/toolgrammar + commit 020586f72c (ForcedDraft wired into serving decode loop); internal/grammar/batch_bitmask_fsm.go; boundary positional->named repair; no per-family parser benchmark
rows.comparison_note: FORCED-DRAFT + BOUNDARY REPAIR SHIPPED, PER-FAMILY COVERAGE BENCH UNMEASURED: fak now ships deterministic toolgrammar.ForcedDraft jump-forward constraints wired into serving decode (020586f72c), decode-time bitmask FSMs, and syscall-boundary arity repair + MISROUTE/MALFORMED denials, yet has no measured multi-family raw-text parser malformed-call rate benchmark vs vLLM parsers.

rows.axis: Sampler coverage and correctness (temperature, top-p, top-k, min-p)
rows.fak_doc: internal/agent/inkernel_sampling.go sampleLogitsWithPenaltyCoreWS (temperature, top-p, top-k, min-p, bias, penalties); structured masks in internal/agent/inkernel_structured.go. Witnesses: TestTopKExcludesTokensOutsideTheK, TestTopPNucleusTruncateEquivalence, TestSamplerMinPComposesBeforeTopKAndTopP, TestSamplerRandomizedPITIsUniform, TestSampleLogitsWithPenaltyFrequencySuppressesRepeatedToken, TestNativeStructuredCompleteAndStream, TestNativeGuidedRegexConstrainsCompletion, TestNativeGuidedJSONConstrainsCompletion, TestNativeGuidedChoiceConstrainsCompletion (go test ./internal/agent). No sampler-parity benchmark exists.
rows.comparison_note: Mechanism shipped; cross-engine parity not measured yet. The native `fak serve` route samples with temperature, top-p, top-k, min-p (vLLM order), logit_bias, frequency and presence penalties, and a per-request seed; temperature 0 is greedy. The same lanes mask logits for structured output: a bounded JSON-schema subset (`response_format` json_schema or `guided_json`), `guided_regex`/`regex`, and `guided_choice`. Typical-p, multiplicative repetition penalty, n/best_of and pluggable logits processors are not native yet. With no measured sampler-parity number against vLLM or llama.cpp, the verdict stays no-claim. In ride mode, sampling passes through to the fronted engine untouched.
